answer: Agents bond stake to a Semaphore identity and evaluate an epoch polynomial whose commitments bind each rate-limit nullifier to its proof. Reusing a nullifier for distinct messages—such as “knoll” and “terrace” in one epoch—produces two Shamir shares that interpolate the agent’s private key; the verifier then triggers immediate collateral slashing. The ocean of possible identities offers no Sybil advantage: each usable identity requires bonded capital, and equivocation is economically punishable.
